title: Neck-to-Shoulder Stroking
summary: A smooth stroke begins at the posterior neck and continues outward along the top line of the shoulders.
goal: Connect neck and shoulder work while gently distributing contact across the upper trapezius.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of stroking from the posterior neck toward the shoulders.
startingPosition: The person lies or sits in a stable position with relaxed shoulders. The hands begin near the base of the neck.
instructions: Place the hands near the base of the neck on either side of the spine.
Continue along the upper shoulders toward the outside.
Gradually reduce pressure near the shoulder joints.
direction: From the base of the neck outward along the upper shoulder line.
tips: Follow the natural contour of the shoulder girdle.
Do not lift the person's shoulders with the movement.
mistakes: Excessive pressure at the base of the neck.
warning: Do not work through acute pain, inflammation, or recent shoulder-girdle injury.
telegramCaption: A smooth transition from the base of the neck outward along the shoulders.
